correctness.rationale: For each of the ten positive ordered triples I reconstructed the nine-vertex tree metric and B_p(i,j)=(d(i,8)^p+d(j,8)^p-d(i,j)^p)/2 for p=137/100. The independent integer-only 100th-root enclosure with denominator 10^12 and outward fixed-point rational interval Schur/LDL elimination certified eight strictly positive pivots only at (2,1,3) and (3,1,2); each other triple has a strictly negative pivot after positive ones. The six reversal classes and all ten ordered triples were checked; this validates the exact finite separation. A strict positive Gram persists to larger p by eigenvalue continuity; a negative pivot at p0 forces its supremal negative-type threshold below p0 by the finite-metric closed initial-interval property. Schoenberg converts these statements to all-scale Gaussian kernels.
